name: chart
purpose: A cartesian chart — lines, areas, stacked areas, bars, mixed bars and lines, and scatter dots over one category axis — composed from parts the consumer places by hand. The root owns the data model (series + labels), the scales, the hover/keyboard state and the loading / empty / error surface; each part (`Chart.Grid`, `Chart.Axis`, `Chart.Brush`, `Chart.Line`, `Chart.Area`, `Chart.Bar`, `Chart.Scatter`, `Chart.Crosshair`, `Chart.Tooltip`, `Chart.Legend`) reads that state through context, so the consumer wires nothing. Rendering is in-house SVG and every color comes from the `--chart-*` role, so a chart re-themes with no per-theme code and adds no charting dependency.
useWhen: A measure over time — requests, threats, bandwidth per bucket — as one or more lines or areas.
Comparing magnitudes across ordered categories — top countries, attack families — as vertical or horizontal bars.
Parts of a total over time — allowed / blocked / logged — as stacked areas or stacked bars.
Any chart that must read the same as Azion Console Real-Time Metrics: crosshair, one tooltip listing every series, legend toggles, totals.
Two measures of one unit where one is the total and one a part — requests as bars, cached requests as a line (mixed).
How one measure spreads against another — response time by object size — as scatter dots on a `linear` label scale.
A volume histogram that filters a log or a table to a time span: add `Chart.Brush` and read `v-model:range`.
avoidWhen: A single headline number with a delta → use `stat-tile`.
Share of a small whole (six slices or fewer) with the total in the center → use `donut-chart`.
More than about seven classes that all carry meaning → use `table`; color stops separating past the six series slots.
Two measures on different scales → two charts side by side; this component never draws a second value axis.
One reading against its range (CPU, cache hit ratio) → use `gauge-chart`.
Values by country or location → use `map-chart`.
related: chart-card` — the box a dashboard chart sits in: title, description, controls, drag and resize.
donut-chart` — part-to-whole at a glance, sharing this chart's palette, legend and states.
stat-tile` — one figure with a delta and a sparkline, for a KPI row above the charts.
table` — the exact numbers; a chart's own table view is the accessible twin, a `table` is the primary surface.
bestPractices: Pass series in a stable order: the slot follows the series position, so color follows the entity. A filter that hides a series keeps the others' colors.
Keep one value axis. Index two measures to a common base or split them into two charts.
Let the legend carry identity for two or more series; a single series needs no legend, its title names it.
Mark a series whose color means a state (blocked, error rate) with `color: 'danger'` and never reuse a status color as series 4.
Color a series that counts one severity level with `color: 'severity-critical'` (`-high`, `-medium`, `-low`, `-info`) so stacked bars and legends match the `SeverityTag` in the table below the chart.
Keep filters and the time range in one row above the dashboard, never inside a chart.

While data reloads, set `refetching` so the previous marks hold at reduced opacity instead of flashing a skeleton. Only the SVG marks dim (`data-[refetching]:[&_svg]:opacity-60`); legend values and other text stay at full contrast, because text at 60% opacity drops `--text-muted` under 4.5:1 (2.78:1 light, 3.14:1 dark).

Place `Chart.Brush` before the marks so the selection band sits under them. The page owns what a range means: bind `range` to `null` and filter on `update:range` when the data changes with the selection.
Use `labelScale="linear"` only with numeric or Date labels; keep `category` for buckets that are evenly spaced.

props.name: series
props.doc: Series to plot. The first six take the fixed categorical slots in order; the rest fold into Other.

props.name: labels
props.doc: One category label per index: a string, a number, or a Date.

props.name: orientation
props.doc: Value axis direction. Horizontal lays categories down the side, for ordered bars.

props.name: labelScale
props.doc: How categories sit along their axis. `linear` places numeric or Date labels by value, for scatter plots and uneven time buckets.

props.name: min
props.doc: Floor of the value axis. Marks grow from one baseline.

props.name: max
props.doc: Ceiling of the value axis. When absent, the nice ceiling of the visible data.

props.name: cap
props.doc: Series kept before the rest fold into Other.

props.name: otherLabel
props.doc: Name of the folded series. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Other`).

props.name: formatValue
props.doc: Formats ticks, tooltip values and legend totals.

props.name: formatLabel
props.doc: Formats category labels on the axis and in the tooltip.

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: IANA time zone the default label format prints Date labels in. Empty prints UTC on the server and in the first client render, then the runtime's zone.

props.name: height
props.doc: Minimum plot height in pixels; the plot grows to fill a taller container.

props.name: loading
props.doc: Renders a Skeleton sized to the plot and suppresses interaction.

props.name: refetching
props.doc: Holds the previous render at reduced opacity while new data loads.

props.name: error
props.doc: Error message; when set, the plot renders a danger Alert instead of marks.

props.name: emptyTitle
props.doc: Title of the empty state shown when no series has a value. Empty uses the locale catalog (`No data available`).

props.name: emptyDescription
props.doc: Supporting line under the empty title: why the range is empty, or what to do next.

props.name: tableView
props.doc: Shows the data table in place of the marks. The table is always present for assistive tech.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: Accessible name of the chart when it is not inside a ChartCard with a title.

events.name: point-click
events.notes: Click on the plot, or Enter / Space on the focused chart, at the active index. `point` carries the index, the label and every visible series value.

events.name: legend-toggle
events.notes: A legend entry toggled; `series` is the consumer's own series object.

slots.name: default
slots.notes: The parts: Grid, Axis, Brush, Line, Area, Bar, Scatter, Crosshair, Tooltip, Legend, in paint order.

slots.name: empty-actions
slots.notes: Actions under the default EmptyState, such as a Clear filters button or a setup link. Ignored when `empty` replaces it.

examples.sfc:
<script setup>
  import Chart from '@aziontech/webkit/chart'

  const labels = [
    '13:05',
    '13:10',
    '13:15',
    '13:20',
    '13:25',
    '13:30',
    '13:35',
    '13:40',
    '13:45',
    '13:50',
    '13:55',
    '14:00'
  ]
  const series = [
    {
      id: 'allowed',
      name: 'WAF requests allowed',
      color: 'success',
      values: [1210, 1340, 1295, 1480, 1530, 1460, 1610, 1580, 1720, 1690, 1810, 1760]
    },
    {
      id: 'blocked',
      name: 'WAF requests blocked',
      color: 'danger',
      values: [320, 410, 380, 520, 470, 430, 610, 580, 540, 690, 650, 720]
    },
    {
      id: 'threat',
      name: 'WAF requests threat',
      color: 'warning',
      values: [80, 95, 70, 120, 110, 90, 140, 130, 115, 160, 150, 170]
    }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <Chart
    :series="series"
    :labels="labels"
    aria-label="Threats vs requests"
  >
    <Chart.Grid />
    <Chart.Axis kind="y" />
    <Chart.Axis kind="x" />
    <Chart.Area :ids="['allowed']" />
    <Chart.Line :ids="['blocked', 'threat']" />
    <Chart.Crosshair />
    <Chart.Tooltip />
    <Chart.Legend totals />
  </Chart>
</template>
